Thin K crust sitting on the basal facets

Surface layer: PP 1.0 mm with secondary DF 0.5 mm

notes: CT28SC: loose facets on the ice , 100 m above the toe on the ice. helicopter access
summary: Glacier-ice pit, 105 cm: basal 0-7 cm loose FCxr facets (4F) under a thin K MFcr crust (7-10 cm), then a thick hard P layer of fine RG (10-55 cm) and softer 1F RG/DF/PP above; CT28 SC at 7 cm (on basal facets), CT5 RP at 77 cm and CT11 RP at 87 cm (both on a '*' PP layer per label)
reading_issues: Same pit in two exports: the PDF is a depth-from-surface chart (0 at top, 'PIT 105' at bottom); the PNG is a height-above-base chart. Heights taken from the PNG (calibrated from pixel geometry) and cross-checked against the PDF (depth converted as 105 - depth); they agree. Header HS is blank ('--'); hs_cm=105 is the chart's total pit/stack height (pit on glacier ice). Hardness-axis tick spacing is non-uniform in the PNG but uniform in the PDF; piecewise-linear interpolation between ticks gives the same hardness in both. Three layers have a tapered (sloping) hardness bar; hardness/hardness_idx for those are layer means and the top/bottom values are in the comment. Basal glyph (rounded-top square) read as FCxr. CT11RP/CT5RP labels give the failure layer as a '*' (PP) 3.0/2.0 mm although the grain table lists DF at 87-100 cm and DF(FC) at 77-87 cm; test heights are the yellow-line heights (87.0, 77.0, 7.0 cm). Temperature dots read from PNG (95 cm down to 10 cm; no surface/ground point). Blowing snow and precip taken from header text.
